KEY MESSAGE 1...Temps continue to moderate Thu with highs reaching 
into the lower-middle 70s in many locations. Mainly dry weather 
continues with a few brief spot showers possible with a cold front. 

High pressure will continue to shift east of the region tonight as a 
cold front approaches from the west on Thursday. A modest southwest 
LLJ ahead of this cold front should keep most locations from 
decoupling tonight. This will result in a much milder night than 
what we saw last night. Overnight low temps should only drop into 
the middle 40s to the lower 50s in most locations with middle 50s in 
the Urban Heat Island of Boston. 

A moisture starved cold front and associated pre-frontal trough will 
be approaching the area from the west near daybreak Thu. This will 
result in a period of mid-level cloudiness and a few brief passing 
showers possible...mainly Thu morning. However...any showers will be 
very short-lived in a given location and pretty much looking at a 
dry day. Otherwise...partial sunshine with 925T around +14C should 
result in high temps mainly in the lower to middle 70s in many 
locations. There is a low risk for a few additional spot showers 
ahead of the cold front too...but again the majority of the day is 
dry. A bit of a breeze out of the west southwest too...but overall a 
very nice day. 

Winds diminish Thu night with skies becoming clear. This will allow 
for a good night of radiational cooling with low temps mainly in the 
40s...but some upper 30s possible in the normally coolest outlying 
locations. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry weather prevails Friday through early Sunday, 
with another frosty start possible Saturday. Rain is increasingly 
likely late Sunday into Columbus Day, though uncertainty remains 
with onset timing and rainfall amounts.

The extended forecast remains on track with no major shifts. Strong 
1030+ mb high pressure builds over the Northeast Friday and 
Saturday, supporting sunny and dry conditions. Highs Friday are 
seasonably cool in the post-frontal airmass, mainly in the lower to 
middle 60s. WAA develops aloft Saturday as 925 mb temperatures 
increase from around +8C Friday to +9C to +12C Saturday, supporting 
highs in the middle 60s to lower 70s. Another frosty start is 
possible Saturday, especially in the typically colder locations 
where light/calm winds favor effective radiational cooling. The NBM 
doesn't capture this particularly well, so blended in MOS guidance, 
resulting in lows in the mid 30s across the colder locations while 
the urban core remains in the mid to upper 40s.

Confidence is high in dry weather Friday through early Sunday given 
strong ensemble agreement on high pressure dominating the Northeast. 
Confidence decreases thereafter with respect to timing and rainfall 
amounts, though it is looking increasingly likely that rain arrives 
sometime late Sunday and continues into Columbus Day. High pressure 
shifts east Sunday as remnant moisture from Isaias begins to 
approach southern New England. Isaias, currently over the southwest 
Gulf, is expected to make landfall Friday night on the Gulf Coast. 
Guidance still shows a fairly wide window for the onset of rain, 
ranging from late Sunday morning to after sunset, but confidence is 
moderate to high that rain occurs Sunday night into Monday.

There are signals that this could be a soaking rain, though 
confidence in amounts remains lower. PWATs increase to 2-3 standard 
deviations above climatology, while DESI probabilities for 0.50+ 
inches of rain from 8 PM Sunday to 8 PM Monday range from around 45 
percent across northern Massachusetts to 60-70 percent along coastal 
Rhode Island and Massachusetts. Probabilities for 2+ inches remain 
low, around 10-15 percent and mainly confined to Block Island, 
Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket.

Forecast confidence becomes quite low by Tuesday, though the pattern 
favors continued unsettled weather as a cold front potentially 
approaches from the west. Otherwise, no significant changes to 
temperatures, with highs generally in the 60s to around 70 Sunday 
through Tuesday and overnight lows in the upper 40s and 50s.
